display: Pharmacist and owner of an independent pharmacy in the Annex, Toronto. I offer MedsCheck medication reviews for seniors.

signals.text: I'm looking for a health-sciences student who wants to learn the profession properly and stay, not someone treating the job as a short stop.
The student assistant position at my pharmacy is open: paid, flexible hours, with real teaching.
I'd like more seniors who take three or more medications to come in for a MedsCheck review, but I have no time for outreach.
I'm renovating the back room into a quiet consultation space and the contractor keeps slipping. I could use a reliable contractor or project-manager perspective.
The counter is chaotic right now and the team is swamped without an extra pair of hands.
I've been tired for weeks and I'm running on little slack.
Cash flow is tight while the renovation drags on.
I'd like to find ways to cut the paperwork load so I can spend more time on conversations with patients.
I'm training for a half-marathon and happiest when I'm running; I'd welcome running partners or club contacts in Toronto.
Neighbours keep asking me about their pets' medications, and I only do people. I wonder who I could point them to.
I'd like to share duplicate-prescription catches with local doctors in a smoother way than ad hoc phone calls.
I want safer checking steps for blister-pack preparation so tired staff are less likely to make errors.

offers.text: MedsCheck medication reviews, funded by the province, for seniors on three or more medications. I look for duplicated or conflicting prescriptions.
Licensed Ontario pharmacist with 22 years of experience, certified to give injections including vaccines.
Blister-pack medication packaging for retirement residences and home-living seniors.
A paid, mentored placement where a health-sciences student learns pharmacy practice at the counter, with the experience of supervising pharmacy students.
Working relationships with neighbourhood family doctors and a visiting nurse program, so I can route a senior's concern to the right clinician.
A consultation room in the pharmacy for private one-on-one conversations (a second quiet room is being built).
Explaining medications in plain language to seniors and their families, face to face.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm helping my 78-year-old mother in the Annex. She takes about six pills a day from two different doctors and has started feeling dizzy. Who can review everything together?
catchers.can: Book a free MedsCheck review, check the full medication list for overlaps and interactions, and contact the prescribing doctors if something doubles up.
catchers.confirm: Does the senior live in Ontario, take three or more regular medications, and have a health card, and can they or a family member visit the pharmacy in person?

catchers.hypo: I'm a second-year health-sciences student looking for a part-time job in a community pharmacy where I'd learn something real, and I plan to stay at least a couple of years.
catchers.can: Offer the open paid, flexible student assistant position and teach them properly on the job.
catchers.confirm: Are they a health-sciences or pharmacy-track student who can commit to staying for a year or more and can work around class hours in Toronto?

catchers.hypo: I run a home-care or visiting-nurse program and many of our clients are confused about their medications. Is there a pharmacist who could partner with us?
catchers.can: Provide MedsCheck reviews and blister-pack packaging for those clients, coordinated with the visiting nurse program I already work with.
catchers.confirm: Are the clients seniors in or near central Toronto who could be served by a pharmacy visit or delivery within pharmacy opening hours?

catchers.hypo: I'm a family doctor and I keep finding that patients get overlapping prescriptions from different specialists. Can a pharmacist help catch these early?
catchers.can: Flag duplicates found in medication reviews directly to the prescriber, as I already do with a neighbourhood doctor who asked me to send them all.
catchers.confirm: Is the prescriber in the Toronto area and willing to take calls or faxes from the pharmacy about specific prescription changes?

catchers.hypo: I'm a pharmacy technician looking for a stable shop with a small team, where I can work with a pharmacist who cares about getting things right.
catchers.can: Pass the contact to my senior technician, who has ten years with the shop and can say whether the team needs one more person, or consider them if budget allows.
catchers.confirm: Is the person a certified or registered pharmacy technician in Ontario who is looking for a long-term role, not a short-term fill?

catchers.hypo: I'm a community organizer for a seniors' group in Toronto. Could a pharmacist give a short talk on medication safety at our centre?
catchers.can: Offer a short medication-safety talk or drop-in MedsCheck sign-up, scheduled outside pharmacy hours.
catchers.confirm: Can the event happen outside the pharmacy's opening hours, in person, in downtown Toronto?

catchers.hypo: I run a half-marathon training group on Saturdays along the lake and we have room for another runner at a steady pace.
catchers.can: Join the training group and possibly bring other runners from the neighbourhood.
catchers.confirm: Does the group train in Toronto at a pace suited to someone preparing for a half-marathon, and at times that don't clash with pharmacy hours?

catchers.hypo: I'm a general contractor or renovation project manager and I can take on a small stalled commercial renovation in a shop.
catchers.can: Talk with them about taking over or supporting the back-room consultation space, if the schedule and cost are workable.
catchers.confirm: Do they work in Toronto, handle small retail or healthcare interior renovations, and have capacity to start within a few weeks?

forbids.text: I will not hire someone who treats the job as temporary.
I cannot close the pharmacy during opening hours for events or meetings.
I prefer face-to-face contact with patients and do not offer remote-only medication reviews.
I only treat people as patients and cannot advise on animal medications.
The budget for part-time help is limited, so I can't offer high pay.
I will not share patient names, records or any personal medical information.

projects.name: MedsCheck outreach
projects.text: Bring more eligible seniors into free MedsCheck reviews so duplicated or conflicting medications are caught earlier, through word of mouth and local partners.
roles_needed: volunteer or student helper for outreach

projects.name: Student pharmacy assistant position
projects.text: A paid, flexible, mentored position for a health-sciences student who wants to learn community pharmacy and stay for the long run.
roles_needed: campus career or placement office contact

policy.t1: When there's a real lead, I can share details of the open student assistant position (paid, flexible hours, long-term commitment wanted), the MedsCheck partnership options, and my working relationships with local doctors and nurses.
policy.t2: Once trust is established and the counterpart is clear, I can share that staffing is stretched, that I'm tired, and that renovation cash flow is tight.
policy.never: Patient names and records, and any personal medical information.
